newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's top court rejects Bhutto petition.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's top court rejects Bhutto petition.

text.p: Pakistan's top court snubbed ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto on Saturday, refusing her petition against her sacking, as massed crowds cheered her at the start of a trip to drum up popular support.
The Supreme Court, for the second time in five days, returned Bhutto's petition against her November 5 dismissal by President Farooq Leghari on charges of corruption and misrule.
It accused her lawyer of raising "frivolous and misconceived" objections to the earlier refusal.
No comment was immediately available from Bhutto, who arrived in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore to be greeted by thousands of supporters.
Ahsan had filed an amended petition in the court on Thursday, deleting portions of the original which the court registrar had criticised as "frivolous and scandalous".

Ahsan said he had refiled the petition to save time, but did not accept that the one submitted earlier contained anything inappropriate. He also wrote to the registrar to record Bhutto's disagreement with the court's rejection of the original.

A letter court registrar M.A. Farooqi sent to Ahsan on Saturday, seen by reporters, said the objections and disagreements raised by the lawyer were "frivolous and misconceived and cannot be allowed to be placed on the record".
The registrar, who said he was acting on behalf of the court, told Ahsan that he could appeal.

The first petition's 42 pages contained blistering criticism of Leghari for dismissing the National Assembly and ousting Bhutto, whose three-year-old adminsitration was replaced by a caretaker government due to hold fresh elections on February 3.
Several thousand people, chanting slogans against Leghari, greeted Bhutto at Lahore railway station, witnesses said.
Some party workers gestured angrily at former cabinet ministers accompanying Bhutto and blamed them for her downfall.
Bhutto, 43, is battling to overturn her dismissal by her one-time close political associate.
She has appealed to the Supreme Court to restore the 217-member National Assembly (lower house) dissolved by Leghari and reinstate her government immediately.
Bhutto has said she will await the court's verdict before deciding whether to fight the February 3 general election.
Bhutto has accuse Leghari of breaking his word not to use controversial presidential powers to dismiss governments.

Leghari, Bhutto's nominee for president after she took power in October 1993, has said she brought Pakistan to the brink of economic and social collapse, and was unable to distinguish between the state and the government.

The caretaker government, led by 80-year-old Meraj Khalid, has vowed to bring undisclosed charges against Bhutto and her husband, Asif Ali Zardari, who has been detained under a broad maintenance of public order law since his wife's overthrow.
